questions.stem: What is the molar mass of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2? [Ca = 40, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: The subscript 2 outside the bracket multiplies everything inside it, so the formula contains one Ca, two O and two H. Molar mass = 40 + 2(16 + 1) = 40 + 34 = 74 g/mol.

distractorRationale.a: The bracket was ignored, giving 40 + 16 + 1 as if the formula were CaOH
distractorRationale.b: Only the hydrogen was doubled, giving 40 + 16 + 2
distractorRationale.d: The calcium was doubled as well, giving 80 + 34

questions.stem: How many moles of carbon dioxide are present in 88 g of CO2? [C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: The molar mass of CO2 is 12 + (2 x 16) = 44 g/mol. Using n = m / M gives n = 88 / 44 = 2 mol. As a check, 88 g is twice 44 g, so it must be twice one mole.

distractorRationale.a: The division was inverted, giving 44 divided by 88
distractorRationale.c: A molar mass of 22 was used, as if only one oxygen atom were present and halved
distractorRationale.d: The molar mass was quoted instead of the number of moles

questions.stem: How many molecules are contained in 0.5 mol of oxygen gas? [NA = 6.02 x 10^23 per mole]
questions.explanation: Number of particles = number of moles x Avogadro constant, so N = 0.5 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 3.01 x 10^23 molecules. Half a mole must contain half of the Avogadro constant, which is a quick way to check the answer.

distractorRationale.a: This is 0.2 of a mole rather than 0.5
distractorRationale.c: This is the number in one full mole, ignoring the 0.5 factor
distractorRationale.d: The 0.5 was used as a multiplier of 2 instead of a half

questions.stem: What is the mass of 0.2 mol of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? [Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: The molar mass of NaOH is 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol. Rearranging n = m / M gives m = n x M = 0.2 x 40 = 8 g. One fifth of a mole must weigh one fifth of 40 g.

distractorRationale.a: 0.1 mol was used instead of 0.2 mol
distractorRationale.c: The molar mass was given as the answer without multiplying by the number of moles
distractorRationale.d: The molar mass was divided by the number of moles instead of multiplied

questions.stem: How many atoms in total are present in 0.1 mol of sulphuric acid, H2SO4? [NA = 6.02 x 10^23 per mole]
questions.explanation: Each molecule of H2SO4 contains 2 + 1 + 4 = 7 atoms. So 0.1 mol of molecules contains 0.7 mol of atoms, and 0.7 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 4.214 x 10^23 atoms.

distractorRationale.a: This is the number of molecules, not atoms, so the seven atoms per molecule were ignored
distractorRationale.b: Only the four oxygen atoms were counted, giving 0.4 mol of atoms
distractorRationale.d: This is one full mole of particles, ignoring both the 0.1 factor and the atom count

questions.stem: Calculate the number of moles of iron atoms in 5.6 g of iron. [Fe = 56]
questions.explanation: Using n = m / M with m = 5.6 g and M = 56 g/mol gives n = 5.6 / 56 = 0.1 mol. Since 5.6 g is one tenth of 56 g, the amount must be one tenth of a mole.

questions.stem: Which of the following samples contains the greatest amount of substance in moles? [H = 1, He = 4, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Work out n = m / M for each. Helium: 8 / 4 = 2 mol. Oxygen: 32 / 32 = 1 mol. Carbon dioxide: 44 / 44 = 1 mol. Water: 18 / 18 = 1 mol. Helium wins because it has by far the smallest molar mass, so the same mass contains far more particles.

distractorRationale.b: 32 g of O2 is exactly one mole, since the molar mass of the diatomic molecule is 32
distractorRationale.c: 44 g of CO2 is exactly one mole
distractorRationale.d: 18 g of water is exactly one mole; the largest mass does not mean the most moles
